name: Sanaipei
tagline:
From Child Marriage Survivor at 10
to Independent Salon Entrepreneur
theReality: Married off at age 10 to a 62-year-old man in Kajiado, enduring severe domestic violence. Became pregnant at 12 and gave birth to her daughter Zawadi after nearly miscarrying from physical abuse.
theTurningPoint: Encountered Malkia's SheRISE initiative at age 15. Malkia facilitated trauma therapy, psychosocial rehabilitation, and enrolled her at Maasai National Polytechnic for vocational cosmetology training.
theOutcome: Now 17, Sanaipei operates her own salon in Kajiado, independently funding her household and securing Zawadi's education.
directQuote: My daughter Zawadi will never know what it means to be exchanged for cows. She will hold a pencil before anything else.

name: Namunyak
tagline:
A Young Mother Reclaiming Her Future
and Defending Girl-Child Agency
theReality: Became a mother at 15 in a conservative pastoralist boma. Abandoned by her spouse upon learning of her 2-year-old daughter Naishorua, facing deep community stigma.
theTurningPoint: Joined the Voices Uncut peer mentorship circles, accessing trauma counseling, community mediation, and peer childcare networks.
theOutcome: Re-enrolled into secondary school, balancing education with motherhood while serving as a peer speaker at community barazas.
directQuote: Being a teen mother does not mean my life has ended. My mind is sharp, and my seat in the classroom is mine.

name: Salome Seeman
tagline:
Unlocking Classroom Fluency
at Moipei Comprehensive School
theReality: Struggled with foundational letter recognition in Grade 3 due to overcrowded classrooms and lack of early-grade remedial support.
theTurningPoint: Enrolled in Malkia’s KUZA Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) cohorts across 7 schools, receiving level-based phonetic instruction.
theOutcome: Progressed from non-reader to confidently reading and comprehending paragraphs and stories, lifting self-esteem and attendance.
directQuote: When you know how to read, the words in the book stop feeling like locked doors.
